walkthroughs.body_html:
Cell Division & Genetics — a core area of GCSE Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Cell Division & Genetics brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Cell Division & Genetics.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Why must DNA replicate before mitosis?
options: To save energy
So each daughter cell gets a complete set
To form new chromosomes
To make ATP

mcqs.q: What is the key difference between mitosis and meiosis?
options: Mitosis and meiosis both produce gametes; they are basically the same.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells; meiosis produces four genetically different haploid cells (gametes).

mcqs.q: What is the key structural difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?
options: Eukaryotes have a membrane-bound nucleus and membrane-bound organelles; prokaryotes do not.
Prokaryotes are always smaller than 1 micrometre and have no cytoplasm.
Prokaryotes have no DNA — that's why they have no nucleus.
Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.

mcqs.q: What does a gene code for?
options: A gene codes for a specific physical feature like eye colour directly.
Typically a polypeptide (protein) — through transcription to mRNA and translation by ribosomes.
Mitosis happens in plants and meiosis happens in animals.
Each gene codes for an organ or body part as a whole.

mcqs.q: One cell undergoes 3 rounds of mitosis. How many cells result?
options: 9 cells
6 cells
7 cells
8 cells

mcqs.q: A skin wound heals as new cells replace damaged ones. Which type of cell division is responsible?
options: Mitosis
Meiosis
Fertilisation
Binary fission of gametes

mcqs.q: One cell divides by mitosis. How do the two daughter cells compare with the parent cell?
options: Genetically identical, with the same number of chromosomes
Genetically different, with half the chromosomes
Genetically identical, with half the chromosomes
Genetically different, with twice the chromosomes

mcqs.q: Why must DNA be copied before a cell divides by mitosis?
options: So each daughter cell receives a complete set of chromosomes
To make the cell produce gametes
To reduce the chromosome number by half
To release energy for division

mcqs.q: Embryonic stem cells can develop into many different cell types. Which best describes their value in medicine?
options: They could replace damaged or diseased specialised cells.
They are already specialised and cannot divide.
They can only become more stem cells, nothing else.
They carry out respiration for the whole body.
